```{r load}
load_one <- function(f) { e <- new.env(); load(f, envir = e); get(ls(e)[1], envir = e) }
nuStudy <- load_one(params$nu_file)
study4  <- load_one(params$study4_file)
repRange <- params$repRange
side <- with(nuStudy[[1]]$res_cases[[1]], xlims_sim[2] - xlims_sim[1])
Wp <- side + 2 * repRange   # side of the enlarged window W' the daughters live on
nu_goal <- nuStudy[[1]]$par_goal$nu
```

```{r helpers}
# Effective sample size of a set of importance weights. Ranges from 1 (one
# realization carries all the weight) to n (all weights equal).
ess <- function(w) sum(w)^2 / sum(w^2)

# K-function contrast, matching the optimizer's objective.
K_contrast <- function(K_true, K_est, q = 1/4) {
  dr <- K_true$r[2] - K_true$r[1]
  sum((K_true$border^q - K_est$border^q)^2) * dr
}

# Relative RMS error in K.
K_relerr_pct <- function(K_true, K_est) {
  100 * sqrt(mean((K_est$border - K_true$border)^2)) / sqrt(mean(K_true$border^2))
}

# kappa, scale and mu are stored on the log scale and nu on its own scale, so a delta
# in nu is additive and the others are log differences.
delta_of <- function(par_0, par_goal) {
  d <- unlist(par_0 - par_goal)
  nz <- names(d)[abs(d) > 1e-8]
  if (length(nz) == 0) return(list(par = "none", value = 0, label = "delta = 0 (par_0 = par_goal)"))
  if (length(nz) > 1) return(list(par = "multiple", value = NA_real_, label = "multiple"))
  label <- if (nz == "nu") sprintf("nu %+.2f (nu_0 = %.2f)", d[[nz]], par_0$nu)
           else sprintf("%s %+.2f (x%.2f)", nz, d[[nz]], exp(d[[nz]]))
  list(par = nz, value = d[[nz]], label = label)
}

fmt_par <- function(p) {
  v <- unlist(p)
  v[c("kappa", "scale", "mu")] <- exp(v[c("kappa", "scale", "mu")])
  paste(sprintf("%s=%.3g", names(v), v), collapse = ", ")
}

# At fixed scale, nu changes the size of the clusters as well as the shape of the
# kernel: a daughter's mean squared distance from its parent is 4*scale^2*(nu + 1).
rms_radius <- function(scale, nu) 2 * scale * sqrt(nu + 1)

# Parent window padding: clusterradius() with spatstat's default thresh = 0.001.
pad_of <- function(scale, nu) spatstat.random::clusterradius("VarGamma", scale = scale, nu = nu, thresh = 0.001)

# Flatten one group (a par_goal with its delta cases) into one row per case.
group_rows <- function(grp, study, group_id) {
  goal <- unlist(grp$par_goal)
  do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(grp$res_cases), function(j) {
    cs <- grp$res_cases[[j]]
    ri <- cs$res_is
    n_last <- length(ri$rho_is)
    d  <- delta_of(cs$par_0, grp$par_goal)
    scale_0 <- exp(cs$par_0$scale)
    nu_0 <- if (is.null(cs$par_0$nu)) cs$nu else cs$par_0$nu
    Kt <- grp$res_true$K_true
    w  <- ri$w_is
    data.frame(
      study = study, group = group_id, case = j,
      delta = d$label, delta_par = d$par, delta_value = d$value,
      goal = fmt_par(grp$par_goal),
      scale_0 = scale_0, nu_0 = nu_0,
      # log change in the rms cluster radius between the simulation and the target
      log_size_change = log(rms_radius(scale_0, nu_0) / rms_radius(exp(goal[["scale"]]), grp$nu)),
      E_parents = exp(cs$par_0$kappa) * (Wp + 2 * pad_of(scale_0, nu_0))^2,
      nSims = length(w),
      ESS = ess(w),
      ESS_pct = 100 * ess(w) / length(w),
      mean_w = mean(w),
      rho_true = grp$res_true$rho_true,
      rho_relerr_norm_pct   = 100 * (ri$rho_is_norm[n_last] - grp$res_true$rho_true) / grp$res_true$rho_true,
      rho_relerr_unnorm_pct = 100 * (ri$rho_is[n_last] - grp$res_true$rho_true) / grp$res_true$rho_true,
      rho_relerr_base_pct   = 100 * (ri$rho_base - grp$res_true$rho_true) / grp$res_true$rho_true,
      K_relerr_norm_pct = K_relerr_pct(Kt, ri$K_is_norm[[n_last]]),
      K_relerr_base_pct = K_relerr_pct(Kt, ri$K_base),
      K_contrast_norm   = K_contrast(Kt, ri$K_is_norm[[n_last]]),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  }))
}
```

```{r rows}
cases <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(nuStudy), function(g) group_rows(nuStudy[[g]], "nu", g)))
cases$label <- sprintf("group %d | %s | ESS=%.3g%%", cases$group, cases$delta, cases$ESS_pct)

# Study 4's scale perturbations, and its unperturbed anchor, for the comparison at
# equal change in cluster size.
s4 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(study4), function(g) group_rows(study4[[g]], "study4", g)))
s4_scale <- s4[s4$delta_par %in% c("none", "scale"), ]
s4_scale$label <- sprintf("study 4, group %d | %s | ESS=%.3g%%", s4_scale$group, s4_scale$delta, s4_scale$ESS_pct)
```

```{r findings}
pert <- cases[cases$delta_par == "nu", ]

# The run of deltas around 0, on either side, over which the ESS stays at least 20%.
ess_range <- function(g, thr = 20) {
  d <- pert[pert$group == g, ]
  d <- d[order(d$delta_value), ]
  neg <- rev(d$delta_value[d$delta_value < 0]); neg_ok <- rev(d$ESS_pct[d$delta_value < 0]) >= thr
  pos <- d$delta_value[d$delta_value > 0];      pos_ok <- d$ESS_pct[d$delta_value > 0] >= thr
  c(lo = if (all(neg_ok)) min(neg) else if (neg_ok[1]) neg[which(!neg_ok)[1] - 1] else 0,
    hi = if (all(pos_ok)) max(pos) else if (pos_ok[1]) pos[which(!pos_ok)[1] - 1] else 0)
}
rng <- lapply(1:2, ess_range)

ess_at <- function(g, dv) pert$ESS_pct[pert$group == g & abs(pert$delta_value - dv) < 1e-8]

usable <- pert$ESS_pct >= 1
max_rho_err <- max(abs(pert$rho_relerr_norm_pct[usable]))
max_rho_base <- max(abs(pert$rho_relerr_base_pct[usable]))
max_K_err <- max(pert$K_relerr_norm_pct[usable])
max_K_base <- max(pert$K_relerr_base_pct[usable])

reliable <- pert$ESS_pct >= 5
mw_range <- range(pert$mean_w[reliable])

# Expected number of parents within one rms cluster radius of a point: how much the
# clusters overlap.
goal_rows <- cases[cases$delta_par == "none", ]
overlap <- sapply(1:2, function(g) {
  p <- exp(unlist(nuStudy[[g]]$par_goal[c("kappa", "scale", "mu")]))
  p[["kappa"]] * pi * rms_radius(p[["scale"]], nu_goal)^2
})

# nu against scale at equal change in cluster size: study 4's scale curve, anchor
# included, interpolated log-linearly at each nu case's size change.
cmp <- do.call(rbind, lapply(1:2, function(g) {
  b <- s4_scale[s4_scale$group == g, ]
  b <- b[order(b$log_size_change), ]
  a <- pert[pert$group == g, ]
  a$ESS_scale_pct <- exp(approx(b$log_size_change, log(b$ESS_pct), a$log_size_change)$y)
  a
}))
cmp$ratio <- cmp$ESS_pct / cmp$ESS_scale_pct
small <- abs(cmp$log_size_change) <= 0.05
larger <- abs(cmp$log_size_change) > 0.05 & cmp$ESS_pct >= 1 & cmp$ESS_scale_pct >= 1
```

This report covers the **study of perturbing $\nu$** for the Variance gamma process (`r basename(params$nu_file)`). It uses the two groups of $(\kappa, \sigma, \mu)$ and the window of the Variance gamma study 4 (`r basename(params$study4_file)`). It holds those three fixed and simulates the ensembles at $\nu_0 = \nu + \delta$ around the target $\nu = `r nu_goal`$.

- **$\nu$ is perturbed additively**, on its own scale rather than the log scale, since it can be negative. The kernel needs $\nu > -1$, but spatstat's `rVarGamma` refuses $\nu \le -1/2$, so the grid stops at $\delta = -0.9$, i.e. $\nu_0 = -0.4$.
- **At fixed $\sigma$, $\nu$ changes the cluster size as well as the shape of the kernel.** A daughter's mean squared distance from its parent is $4\sigma^2(\nu + 1)$, so the rms cluster radius is $2\sigma\sqrt{\nu + 1}$. The section [comparing with the scale](#vs-scale) uses this to separate the two effects.
- **Only the daughter part of the weight changes.** With $\kappa$ fixed, the parent density is the same for the ensemble and the target and cancels, even though the parent window $B$ grows with $\nu_0$.

**ESS** is the effective sample size $\left(\sum w_i\right)^2 / \sum w_i^2$, and `ESS_pct` is it as a percentage of `nSims`.

```{r design-table}
design <- do.call(rbind, lapply(1:2, function(g) {
  p <- exp(unlist(nuStudy[[g]]$par_goal[c("kappa", "scale", "mu")]))
  data.frame(group = g, kappa = p[["kappa"]], scale = p[["scale"]], mu = p[["mu"]], nu = nu_goal,
             rms_radius = rms_radius(p[["scale"]], nu_goal),
             E_daughters = p[["kappa"]] * p[["mu"]] * Wp^2,
             overlap = overlap[g],
             rho_true = nuStudy[[g]]$res_true$rho_true)
}))
knitr::kable(design, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,
             col.names = c("group", "kappa", "scale", "mu", "nu", "rms cluster radius",
                           "E[unthinned daughters]", "parents within one rms radius", "true intensity"),
             caption = "The two groups at their target parameters. The last but one column is the expected number of parents within one rms cluster radius of a point, a measure of how much the clusters overlap.")
```

# Main findings

- **Importance sampling handles $\nu$ well over a useful range.** The ESS stays at or above 20% for $\delta$ from `r rng[[1]][["lo"]]` to `r rng[[1]][["hi"]]` in group 1, and from `r rng[[2]][["lo"]]` to `r rng[[2]][["hi"]]` in group 2. Among the cases with an ESS of at least 1%, the self-normalized estimates are within `r sprintf("%.2f", max_rho_err)`% of the true intensity and `r sprintf("%.2f", max_K_err)`% (relative RMS) of the true K-function. Simply ignoring the weights leaves errors of up to `r sprintf("%.1f", max_rho_base)`% and `r sprintf("%.2f", max_K_base)`% there.
- **The weights are unbiased.** In every case with an ESS of at least 5%, the mean raw weight lies between `r sprintf("%.3f", mw_range[1])` and `r sprintf("%.3f", mw_range[2])`.
- **Simulating at a smaller $\nu$ than the target costs more than a larger one.** At $\delta = -0.4$ the ESS is `r sprintf("%.1f", ess_at(1, -0.4))`% and `r sprintf("%.1f", ess_at(2, -0.4))`% (groups 1 and 2), against `r sprintf("%.1f", ess_at(1, 0.4))`% and `r sprintf("%.1f", ess_at(2, 0.4))`% at $+0.4$. At $\pm 0.8$ it is `r sprintf("%.2f", ess_at(1, -0.8))`% and `r sprintf("%.2f", ess_at(2, -0.8))`% against `r sprintf("%.1f", ess_at(1, 0.8))`% and `r sprintf("%.1f", ess_at(2, 0.8))`%. This is the usual rule that the simulation distribution should have the heavier tails. The kernel's tail behaves like $r^{\nu - 1/2} e^{-r/\sigma}$, so a smaller $\nu_0$ gives a lighter tail and smaller clusters, and the weights grow for the daughters furthest from their parents.
- **Group 2 tolerates much larger shifts than group 1.** Its clusters overlap far more: a point has `r sprintf("%.1f", overlap[2])` parents within one rms cluster radius in group 2, against `r sprintf("%.1f", overlap[1])` in group 1. The intensity at a daughter is then a sum over many parents' kernels, and that sum changes less with the kernel's shape than a single kernel does. The same pattern holds for the scale in study 4.
- **A $\nu$ shift costs about as much as a scale shift of the same size change for small shifts, and more beyond that.** For changes of up to 0.05 in the log rms radius, the ESS of a $\nu$ shift is `r sprintf("%.2f", min(cmp$ratio[small]))` to `r sprintf("%.2f", max(cmp$ratio[small]))` times that of a scale shift with the same change in cluster size. For larger changes it is `r sprintf("%.2f", min(cmp$ratio[larger]))` to `r sprintf("%.2f", max(cmp$ratio[larger]))` times, so there the change of shape adds to the degeneracy.

# Per-case results

One row per (group, case), evaluated at the largest `nSamples`. Rows are shaded where the normalized intensity estimate is more than 10% off, and where ESS falls below 1% of `nSims`.

```{r case-table}
show <- cases[, c("group","case","delta","delta_value","nu_0","log_size_change","E_parents","nSims",
                  "ESS","ESS_pct","mean_w",
                  "rho_relerr_norm_pct","rho_relerr_unnorm_pct","rho_relerr_base_pct",
                  "K_relerr_norm_pct","K_relerr_base_pct","K_contrast_norm")]
datatable(show, rownames = FALSE, filter = "top",
          options = list(pageLength = 25, scrollX = TRUE,
                         order = list(list(0, "asc"), list(3, "asc")))) |>
  formatRound(c("ESS", "E_parents"), 1) |>
  formatRound(c("delta_value", "nu_0"), 2) |>
  formatRound("log_size_change", 3) |>
  formatSignif(c("ESS_pct", "mean_w"), 3) |>
  formatRound(c("rho_relerr_norm_pct","rho_relerr_unnorm_pct","rho_relerr_base_pct",
                "K_relerr_norm_pct","K_relerr_base_pct"), 2) |>
  formatSignif("K_contrast_norm", 3) |>
  formatStyle("rho_relerr_norm_pct",
              backgroundColor = styleInterval(c(-10, 10), c("#f8d7da", "white", "#f8d7da"))) |>
  formatStyle("ESS_pct", backgroundColor = styleInterval(1, c("#f8d7da", "white")))
```

`E_parents` is the expected number of parents per pattern at $\nu_0$. It grows with $\nu_0$ because spatstat pads the parent window further for a heavier-tailed kernel. It does not enter the weights here, since the parent density cancels when $\kappa$ is not perturbed, but it does set how long each case took to simulate.

# ESS against the perturbation

```{r ess-vs-delta}
grp_col <- c("#1b7837", "#762a83")
p <- plot_ly()
for (g in 1:2) {
  d <- cases[cases$group == g, ]
  d <- d[order(d$delta_value), ]
  p <- p |> add_trace(x = d$delta_value, y = d$ESS_pct, type = "scatter", mode = "lines+markers",
                      name = sprintf("group %d", g), text = d$label, hoverinfo = "text",
                      line = list(color = grp_col[g]), marker = list(color = grp_col[g], size = 8))
}
p |> layout(xaxis = list(title = "delta in nu (nu_0 = nu + delta)", zeroline = TRUE),
            yaxis = list(title = "ESS as % of nSims", type = "log"))
```

# Compared with perturbing the scale {#vs-scale}

At fixed $\sigma$ a change in $\nu$ also changes the cluster size, so a $\nu$ shift is part size change and part shape change. Study 4 perturbed the scale, which changes only the size. The plot puts both on a common axis, the log change in rms cluster radius between the simulation and the target: $\tfrac12\log\frac{\nu_0 + 1}{\nu + 1}$ for a $\nu$ shift, and the log-delta itself for a scale shift. Where the $\nu$ curve lies below the scale curve, the change of shape costs ESS on top of the size change. Study 4's scale grid is coarse ($\pm 0.1, 0.2, 0.4, 0.8$), so the comparison in the findings interpolates between its points.

```{r vs-scale}
p <- plot_ly()
for (g in 1:2) {
  d <- cases[cases$group == g, ];    d <- d[order(d$log_size_change), ]
  b <- s4_scale[s4_scale$group == g, ]; b <- b[order(b$log_size_change), ]
  p <- p |>
    add_trace(x = d$log_size_change, y = d$ESS_pct, type = "scatter", mode = "lines+markers",
              name = sprintf("group %d, nu shifted", g), text = d$label, hoverinfo = "text",
              line = list(color = grp_col[g]), marker = list(color = grp_col[g], size = 8)) |>
    add_trace(x = b$log_size_change, y = b$ESS_pct, type = "scatter", mode = "lines+markers",
              name = sprintf("group %d, scale shifted (study 4)", g), text = b$label, hoverinfo = "text",
              line = list(color = grp_col[g], dash = "dot"),
              marker = list(color = grp_col[g], size = 8, symbol = "diamond-open"))
}
p |> layout(xaxis = list(title = "log change in rms cluster radius (simulation vs target)"),
            yaxis = list(title = "ESS as % of nSims", type = "log"))
```

# Convergence against sample size {.tabset}

Each panel shows how the estimate moves as `nSamples` grows, for the unnormalized and self-normalized weighting schemes. Use the dropdown at the top right to switch between perturbation cases.

```{r conv-funs}
conv_plot <- function(grp, what = c("rho", "K")) {
  what <- match.arg(what)
  labels <- vapply(grp$res_cases,
                   function(cs) delta_of(cs$par_0, grp$par_goal)$label, character(1))
  p <- plot_ly(); idx <- 0; trace_of <- list()

  for (i in seq_along(grp$res_cases)) {
    ri <- grp$res_cases[[i]]$res_is
    if (what == "rho") {
      y_u <- ri$rho_is; y_n <- ri$rho_is_norm
    } else {
      Kt <- grp$res_true$K_true
      y_u <- vapply(ri$K_is,      function(k) K_contrast(Kt, k), numeric(1))
      y_n <- vapply(ri$K_is_norm, function(k) K_contrast(Kt, k), numeric(1))
    }
    p <- p |> add_lines(x = grp$nSamples, y = y_u, name = "unnormalized",
                        legendgroup = "u", line = list(color = "firebrick", dash = "dot"),
                        visible = (i == 1))
    idx <- idx + 1; trace_of[[paste0(i, "u")]] <- idx
    p <- p |> add_lines(x = grp$nSamples, y = y_n, name = "normalized",
                        legendgroup = "n", line = list(color = "steelblue"),
                        visible = (i == 1))
    idx <- idx + 1; trace_of[[paste0(i, "n")]] <- idx
  }

  if (what == "rho") {
    rt <- grp$res_true$rho_true
    p <- p |> add_lines(x = range(grp$nSamples), y = c(rt, rt), name = "rho_true",
                        line = list(color = "black", dash = "dash"), visible = TRUE)
    idx <- idx + 1
    yaxis <- list(title = "intensity estimate")
  } else {
    yaxis <- list(title = "K contrast vs truth (log scale)", type = "log")
  }
  n_total <- idx

  buttons <- lapply(seq_along(grp$res_cases), function(i) {
    vis <- rep(FALSE, n_total)
    vis[trace_of[[paste0(i, "u")]]] <- TRUE
    vis[trace_of[[paste0(i, "n")]]] <- TRUE
    if (what == "rho") vis[n_total] <- TRUE
    list(method = "restyle", args = list("visible", vis), label = labels[i])
  })

  p |> layout(xaxis = list(title = "nSamples", type = "log"), yaxis = yaxis,
              updatemenus = list(list(active = 0, x = 1, y = 1.15,
                                      xanchor = "right", buttons = buttons)))
}
```

```{r conv, results="asis"}
# print()ing a widget inside a results='asis' loop does not register its JS
# dependencies on its own; knit_meta_add() does that explicitly.
for (g in seq_along(nuStudy)) {
  grp <- nuStudy[[g]]
  cat(sprintf("\n## Group %d: %s {.tabset}\n\n", g, fmt_par(grp$par_goal)))
  for (w in c("rho", "K")) {
    cat(sprintf("\n### %s\n\n", if (w == "rho") "Intensity" else "K contrast"))
    pl <- conv_plot(grp, w)
    knitr::knit_meta_add(htmltools::findDependencies(pl))
    print(htmltools::tagList(pl))
  }
}
```

# Estimation error

## Against ESS

```{r err-vs-ess}
p <- plot_ly()
for (g in 1:2) {
  d <- pert[pert$group == g, ]
  p <- p |>
    add_markers(x = d$ESS_pct, y = abs(d$rho_relerr_norm_pct), text = d$label, hoverinfo = "text",
                name = sprintf("group %d, |rho error|", g),
                marker = list(size = 8, opacity = 0.8, color = grp_col[g], symbol = "circle")) |>
    add_markers(x = d$ESS_pct, y = d$K_relerr_norm_pct, text = d$label, hoverinfo = "text",
                name = sprintf("group %d, K relative RMS error", g),
                marker = list(size = 8, opacity = 0.8, color = grp_col[g], symbol = "square-open"))
}
p |> layout(xaxis = list(title = "ESS as % of nSims", type = "log"),
            yaxis = list(title = "relative error of the normalized estimate (%)", type = "log"))
```

## How far does importance sampling have to move the estimate?

The baseline is the error of the **unweighted** ensemble, i.e. what you would get by ignoring the weights entirely. Since the cluster size grows with $\nu_0$, the unweighted intensity and K-function move steadily away from the truth as $|\delta|$ grows, which gives the weights something to correct. Points below the dashed line are cases where the weights improved on the unweighted baseline; points above it are cases where reweighting made the estimate worse.

```{r base-vs-is}
p <- plot_ly()
for (g in 1:2) {
  d <- pert[pert$group == g, ]
  p <- p |>
    add_markers(x = abs(d$rho_relerr_base_pct), y = abs(d$rho_relerr_norm_pct), text = d$label,
                hoverinfo = "text", name = sprintf("group %d, intensity", g),
                marker = list(size = 8, opacity = 0.8, color = grp_col[g], symbol = "circle")) |>
    add_markers(x = d$K_relerr_base_pct, y = d$K_relerr_norm_pct, text = d$label,
                hoverinfo = "text", name = sprintf("group %d, K-function", g),
                marker = list(size = 8, opacity = 0.8, color = grp_col[g], symbol = "square-open"))
}
p |>
  add_lines(x = c(1e-3, 1e3), y = c(1e-3, 1e3), name = "no improvement",
            line = list(color = "grey", dash = "dash")) |>
  layout(xaxis = list(title = "|error| of unweighted baseline (%)", type = "log"),
         yaxis = list(title = "|error| after importance sampling (%)", type = "log"))
```

# Unnormalized weights

At the full sample size the unnormalized estimate is the normalized one multiplied by the mean raw weight, so a mean raw weight of 1 means unnormalized importance sampling is unbiased. The plot shows the cases with an ESS of at least 5%; below that, the sample mean of the weights scatters too much to say anything.

```{r mean-w}
mw <- pert[pert$ESS_pct >= 5, ]
p <- plot_ly()
for (g in 1:2) {
  d <- mw[mw$group == g, ]
  d <- d[order(d$delta_value), ]
  p <- p |> add_trace(x = d$delta_value, y = d$mean_w, type = "scatter", mode = "lines+markers",
                      name = sprintf("group %d", g), text = d$label, hoverinfo = "text",
                      line = list(color = grp_col[g]), marker = list(color = grp_col[g], size = 8))
}
p |>
  add_lines(x = range(mw$delta_value), y = c(1, 1), name = "1",
            line = list(color = "grey", dash = "dash")) |>
  layout(xaxis = list(title = "delta in nu (nu_0 = nu + delta)"),
         yaxis = list(title = "mean raw weight"))
```
